answer: Each verified identity must complete its own chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next. GPUs may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot substantially shorten the delay for one chain; simulating many clones therefore requires proportionally more work and hardware, imposing a physical time-and-resource bottleneck. The ledge is that this deters cheap Sybil creation, not unlimited cloning—a fable would claim otherwise. A Wesolowski proof lets a verifier check completion efficiently without replaying the thread.
